findings: Full changelog confirms explicit policy changes rather than a single timeless suppression promise: 2.9 skipped startup replay; 2.15.5-rc.1 restores one-time indexing while later changes remain muted. Main refreshTocMountSources validates parsed managed/external candidates against persisted and previously accepted mount paths. Earlier parser-only virtual-overlap gaps are mitigated at this caller. IDs and option-type validation remain separate questions; full main/test review incomplete.

Main saves hasSeenOnboarding before opening WelcomeModal, so closing the modal without the explicit dismissal callback does not by itself make onboarding repeat. This resolves the earlier modal-only uncertainty.

Original bindManagedTocSource and writeManagedTocMounts overwrite the target with the current draft before refresh/read. Stateful in-memory controls demonstrate that an empty current draft replaces existing destination mounts with an empty array, and a nonempty old draft replaces rather than merges destination entries. No real files modified.

On synthetic write failure, bind restores managed source fields but leaves the destination removed from settings.tocSources. Original-method isolated control confirms in-memory rollback is partial; subsequent persistence/native UI consequences not run.

Targeted upstream test waits for bound TOC loading before Add, but fs.readFile is independently mocked to return a destination even after fs.writeFile. This test does not model read-after-write coherence and cannot disprove observed replacement. Existing test source read, not executed.

The reviewed main section serializes updateMount operations per mount ID and uses revision checks for TOC resolution; this does not establish global atomicity for all add/migrate/bind operations. writeManagedTocMounts writes directly, without a temporary-file/rename transaction. No production code port.
